newsitem.title: USA: Milwaukee stadium tax challenge in appeals court.
newsitem.headline: Milwaukee stadium tax challenge in appeals court.

text.p: Milwaukee taxpayers challenging the legality of a sales tax used to back bonds for a new Brewers stadium took their case to the U.S. Court of Appeals in Chicago on Wednesday.
A federal judge in Wisconsin had dismissed their lawsuit last fall, finding that the Wisconsin Supreme Court had already upheld the constitutionality of the 0.1 percent five-county sales tax.
Attorney Douglas Bartley told the three-judge panel, however, that "peculiar" and "exasperating" turns in the litigation had resulted ultimately in a violation of due process for the taxpayers.
By limiting the number of pages allowed for the challenge, and shortening the deadline for briefs by five days, the Wisconsin Supreme Court dealt "crushing" blows to the taxpayers, Bartley contended.

While the courts had dismissed the challenges, they did not reach the merits of the case, Bartley contended. The appeals court, then, should return the case to a different federal judge for an immediate ruling on the merits and also halt spending on the stadium until the case is resolved, he said.

But attorney Jon Axelrod, representing the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District and other defendants joined in the lawsuit, told the panel that the Wisconsin Supreme Court already decided the merits of the taxpayer challenge.
"This case is over and done with and they can't get another kick at the cat," Axelrod told the panel.

The district is entitled to proceed with construction on the stadium unfettered, Axelrod said. Every court has page limitations and the ability to set briefing schedules in an expedited matter, he added.
The sales tax is being used to back $160 million of tax-exempt bonds for the stadium, which has been estimated to cost about $250 million.
The judges took the matter under advisement on Wednesday afternoon and adjourned.
